newsitem.title: RUSSIA: FOCUS-LUKoil delays sale, ignores govt cash crunch.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-LUKoil delays sale, ignores govt cash crunch.

text.p: Russia's largest oil company, LUKoil, said on Friday it would probably push back plans to sell a government-owned 15 percent stake to 1998.

"It is better to sell the 15 percent when the company is fully audited by U.S. standards," spokesman Pyotr Neyev told Reuters, adding that company accounts audited to Western standards would probably not be ready this year.
"We will opt probably to sell the 15 percent not in 1997 but in 1998."
Only Thursday, the head of the government privatisation programme said that the stake, worth more than $1.5 billion at current market rates, would be sold this year.

LUKoil share prices have almost tripled in the last year but the company says it needs to finish three years of international standard accounts to assure investors and get the highest possible price for its stock.
It raised new investment funds on Thursday when shareholders authorised issuing 10 million preferred shares worth approximately $110 million to be used to fund a company oil acquisition programme.
The Russian government is desperate for cash to bolster its 1997 budget. It is already slashing spending after receipts through April were 30 percent below target.

Privatisation minister Alfred Kokh said on Thursday he planned to almost double targeted 1997 privatisation revenues to 11.5 trillion roubles ($2 billion) and reiterated that he wanted to sell 15 percent of LUKoil this year.
LUKoil Vice-President Leonid Fedun had told Reuters in February that the stake could be sold this year.
Proceeds from the sale will be divided between Russia and LUKoil, though no details have been released.
"Probably what Kokh said about this year, probably he was not aware of the balance sheet situation, that's all," Neyev said.

LUKoil wants to sell the 15 percent by issuing level-three American Depositary Receipts (ADRs), which are U.S.-traded share-look alikes. The ADR plan would require three years of audited accounts to back the plan.

"We have the full understanding of the state privatisation committee about this and the state is interested in selling the stock for a higher price with a full balance sheet ready and we are negotiatating," Neyev said.

Neyev said LUKoil would also issue convertible bonds backed by oil exports this year. Oil exports from the Caspian Pipeline Consortium, in which LUKoil has a stake, would back the paper, which would be sold to foreign investors, he said.
"The preliminary plan is that LUKoil in 1997 is going to issue convertible bonds...They will be convertible not into shares of LUKoil but into oil," he said.
The cash-hungry government treasury may also get funds from a separate sale of a chunk of Russia's -- and one of the world's -- largest oil companies in terms of oil reserves.
LUKoil is about to auction a five percent government-owned stake which it manages. It extended a $35 million loan to the government in 1995 for temporary control of the stake.
The state will get 70 percent of all proceeds over the original value of the loan, and the market value of the shares is more than $500 million.
But former government-owned-stakes held in trust have fetched below-market stakes at auction and the starting price on the LUKoil stake is only $43 million.
--Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520 ($1 = 5,750 roubles)
